causeScope: Original loader-spelling identity check wrongly rejected the recorded valid full-path lookup because loader GetModuleFileName spelling was System32 while OS-selected WOW64 path was SysWOW64. This explains the recorded R58 ordinal/E_ACCESSDENIED branch; R56 registry failures are separate and untouched. No unique SDK/import-library attribution is asserted.
nativeIdentityContract: Full OS-selected DOS Ole32 path remains the only GetModuleHandleEx(PIN) source. No LoadLibrary, basename, export-address/FROM_ADDRESS selection, search changes or additional native owner.

Before PIN obtain only that path drive current target via QueryDosDeviceW; first MULTI_SZ item only. Reject zero/truncation/invalid bounded metadata, malformed terminators and empty current target. Never authorize historical target entries.

K32GetMappedFileNameW uses actual pinned HMODULE image base and borrowed current-process pseudo handle; returns actual mapped image NT name. No CreateFile, mapping, new file/process handle or close obligation is introduced.

Compare current drive target plus exact OS-chosen DOS suffix against complete mapped NT image name with Windows Unicode ordinal ignore-case. No System32/SysWOW64 replacement, basename or prefix match.
Read current drive mapping again before creating release capability and require the full NT expectation unchanged; final mapping change fails closed.
All path/mapping buffers remain fixed1024 UTF16 units; bound/truncation/NUL checks remain. OnceLock, single intentional process-lifetime PIN, failure caching and typed system free ABI are unchanged.
Loader GetModuleFileName is now cfg(test) diagnostic only; it is not treated as mapped file identity.

testSource.changes: All six existing purposes retained; actual module identity assertions now compare mapped NT paths. Verbose zero-array diagnostic removed in favor of bounded valid path-slice logging. Added wrong-volume/folder/module/current-vs-prior/changed-drive and malformed/oversized metadata tests. Alloc/free pairing still resolves both names from same pinned Ole32, not generated bindings.

primary.supports: Loaded format can retain long/short or special-prefix spelling. Its string is not required to be physical mapped path identity.
Maps an address to actual mapped filename. K32 entry exported by Kernel32 starting Win7/Server2008R2; fixed buffers and zero/full failures checked.
Only queried drive, not enumeration; first MULTI_SZ string current, later strings prior mappings; Kernel32 WindowsXP+. Requery does not mutate mappings.
Official example relates mapped NT device-name paths to QueryDosDevice drive mapping. This candidate uses an already-loaded image and creates no sample file/map owners.

features: Existing Win32_System_ProcessStatus and Win32_Storage_FileSystem already cover both new APIs. No extra Cargo/lock/dependency change beyond first Win32_Globalization addition.
limitations: New K32/QueryDosDevice native behavior and exact NT equality remain NOT_RUN until parent owned real test; original failed source and raw diagnostic are preserved.

The mapping comparison proves complete OS-observed image path relation under current OS drive/object namespace, not DLL content signing or resistance to a malicious administrator rewriting protected system files.
Arbitrary UNC/SUBST/unsupported device target mappings are not silently normalized. System path construction remains the existing local drive OS target.
Modern/Win7 MSVC all22 actual import proofs and Win7/10/11/Seewo runtime evidence remain separate pending gates.
The previous documentation draft describes old loader-path comparison and must be revised to mapped NT identity before merging.
operations: Only R58 independent owned source and evidence edits; rustfmt/diff/metadata architecture only. No Cargo build/test/clippy, Windows/SSH, CI, main edits or Git commit.
